card.occupation: Operations administrator at a small freight forwarding firm near the Port of Felixstowe. She handles booking paperwork, chases customs documents and answers the phones, working full-time, about 37.5 hours a week.
card.education_detail: GCSEs at a comprehensive in Ipswich, then a two-year BTEC National in Business and Finance at Suffolk College. Later she did an NVQ Level 3 in Business Administration through work in her late twenties. She never went to university and doesn't feel she missed much.
card.household: Lives with her husband Dean (51, self-employed electrician) in a three-bed semi on the east side of Ipswich. Their son Callum (24) moved out two years ago and lives in Norwich with his girlfriend. They have an elderly, slightly overweight Staffordshire bull terrier called Bramble.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Ipswich to a dad who worked at the docks and a mum who was a dinner lady. She was christened and confirmed Church of England and went to Brownies at the church hall. She still calls herself Christian and means it in a quiet way. She goes to the local parish church at Christmas, Easter and for the odd family christening, and says a prayer when things go wrong. Most of her family are still within twenty minutes' drive.
card.professional_persona: The person everyone at work likes and the one most likely to say 'oh god, did I not send that?' She is warm and patient with drivers, customers and agents, and good at calming down a stressed client on the phone. Her desk is a mess of sticky notes and half-drunk mugs, and she runs on last-minute catch-ups and the goodwill she has built up. Her manager knows her filing is chaotic but keeps her because people trust her and she will cover anyone's shift if asked.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks Bramble round Christchurch Park or along the Orwell at weekends. She has joined and abandoned two gyms and a Couch to 5K app. She follows Ipswich Town loosely because Dean is a season ticket holder, and she got genuinely excited about the promotion.
card.arts_persona: She watches a lot of telly: Strictly, Bake Off, crime dramas and anything with Sheridan Smith. She reads the odd thriller on holiday and rarely finishes it. She goes to the Regent Theatre for a panto or a touring musical once or twice a year, usually booked by her sister.
card.travel_persona: Mostly a package-holiday person. That means a week somewhere warm like Lanzarote, Crete or the Algarve, plus long weekends in a caravan at Walton-on-the-Naze or Southwold. She always means to plan earlier and always ends up booking a late deal. She went to New York once for her 40th and still talks about it.
card.culinary_persona: A cook of comfortable family meals: shepherd's pie, spag bol, a roast on Sundays when Callum visits. Midweek it's often something quick from the freezer or a takeaway on Friday. She says 'dinner' and occasionally 'tea' without thinking about it. She bakes a decent Victoria sponge for birthdays and drinks too much tea at work.
hobbies_and_interests: walking the dog along the river
Facebook groups for local news and lost pets
the odd quiz night at the local pub with friends
half-finished craft projects (a cross-stitch started in 2021)
helping out at the church Christmas fair
skills: calming down upset or angry callers
getting people to do favours for her
Excel basics and the company's booking system
remembering everyone's kids' names and birthdays
improvising when paperwork has gone missing
card.career_goals: Not especially ambitious. She'd like a small pay rise and maybe the title of office supervisor, mostly because she does the job informally already. She occasionally wonders about moving to a school office for the holidays, but hasn't looked into it properly. Mainly she wants to keep things steady until retirement and help Callum if he buys a house.
card.voice: Friendly, chatty Suffolk/Ipswich accent, neutral rather than broad, with a slightly quick pace when she warms up. She uses 'erm' a fair bit at the start of answers and 'sort of' as a softener, and ends sentences with 'you know' or 'yeah'. She'll say 'sorry, can you say that again?' if a question is long. She laughs easily, often at herself ('I'm useless, me'). She doesn't like silence and will fill it with a bit of extra detail or a little joke. Words like 'shattered', 'mate' and 'chuffed' come up naturally.
card.typing: Quick and a bit careless. She often starts in lowercase, misses some apostrophes (dont, im) but not all, and uses commas instead of full stops. She'll add 'lol' or a smiley ':)' when she's being friendly. There are the odd typos she doesn't go back to fix, and she rarely writes more than a line or two.
card.with_strangers: Warm and easy to talk to almost straight away. She apologises a lot and is keen to be helpful and give the 'right' answer. She'll chat about the dog or the weather to break the ice. She's a bit self-deprecating about her own organisation and memory.
small_things: the A14 traffic being a nightmare again
Dean's van being parked across the drive
the price of the weekly shop at Tesco
a nice bit of sun at Felixstowe on her lunch break
deeper_things: Worry about her mum, who has started getting forgetful
Missing Callum more than she lets on since he moved out
Feeling a bit embarrassed that she's never been 'organised' like her sister
A quiet faith she leans on more than she admits, especially after her dad died five years ago
Sometimes wondering whether she settled too easily in her job
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot from slightly below, framing her head and shoulders at a kitchen table. Daylight comes from a window to her left, with a ceiling light on making the right side warmer. She has a round, friendly face, light skin with a few freckles and faint laugh lines, and is smiling with her mouth slightly open as if mid-sentence. Her shoulder-length highlighted blonde hair has darker roots showing and is tucked behind one ear. She wears a navy cardigan over a striped top, has small silver hoop earrings and no glasses. Behind her is a cream kitchen with a wall calendar from a local Chinese takeaway, a fridge covered in magnets and a photo of a young man in a graduation gown, and a cluttered worktop with a kettle, a fruit bowl holding two bananas and a pile of post. The edge of a dog bed is just visible on the floor at the bottom right.
